elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: Total external debt generally rose from 2015 to 2025, with a small dip before the final year. It was lowest at the start and highest in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type

elements.description: The 2025 external debt total is divided into public and publicly guaranteed debt and short-term debt, then public debt is broken down by creditor type. Multilateral creditors account for the largest share, with World Bank-IDA the largest named creditor. Within bilateral debt, other bilateral creditors are the largest segment and China is the smallest.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show debt and debt-service ratios from 2015 to 2025 against shaded ranges for DRS reporting countries. In 2025 external debt relative to exports was the highest printed ratio, while debt service relative to GNI was the lowest. The displayed change was positive for external debt / GNI and negative for the other three ratios.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes present average commitment terms for 2025. The Official creditors box shows maturity of 42 years, a grace period of 9 years, and an interest rate of 0.8%, with small horizontal bars below the labels. The Private creditors box shows '..' for maturity, grace period, and interest rate, with empty bars.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
